mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, market expectations for future rate cuts increase, lowering the discount rate applied to equity present values and thereby driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: FOMC holds or cuts rates after a restrictive stance
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during qualifying FEDFUNDS windows, or the 5.25% threshold is not met for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with low unemployment
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day forward returns during qualifying PAYEMS/UNRATE regime, or the interaction is not statistically significant (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months predicts rising investor optimism about future economic activity, which elevates equity risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during qualifying GDPC1 growth periods, or the 2% monthly threshold is not met for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 0.2% month-over-month), suggesting weak demand and tighter supply conditions, which depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% AND CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO/CPIAUCSL moves, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the interaction is not significant (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the monthly RSAFS index over four consecutive months indicate growing demand for safe assets, consistent with a tightening financial conditions channel that compresses equity discount rates and yields negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases for four consecutive months
regime_hint: Financial market stress with rising risk aversion
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during qualifying RSAFS declines, or the four-month decline pattern is not observed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) remains flat for two months signals a tight labor market, prompting central bank rate hikes and compressing equity valuations, which results in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS unchanged for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market tightness with stable employment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during qualifying UNRATE/PAYEMS regime, or the interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly surge in housing starts (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a narrative signal) coincides with a rise in consumer sentiment proxies (not available here) and precedes a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return, suggesting early cycle acceleration that markets anticipate.
regime_hint: Early stage of economic cycle expansion
failure_condition: No significant positive 5-day forward returns during the window following the housing start surge (if observable), or the mechanism is not empirically detectable with available proxies.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below trend, coupled with a sustained rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL > 0.3% monthly for two months), indicate persistent supply-side weakness that elevates inflation expectations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO below trend for two months AND CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Persistent supply disruption with rising inflation expectations
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO/CPIAUCSL moves, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the interaction is not statistically significant.
